readinessLine: Your readiness check: your agent runs on its own, in your repo or as a cloud bot with its own browser and your logins. These ten questions set the limits it runs inside, the same ones an insurer asks before covering it. Answers save as you type. Each question says what the record can show you, and what no one can.
copyAllLead: Below are my ten standing questions for an unattended AI agent, each with what the tape can and cannot measure, and my answers so far, some only rough comments. Read my repo, then turn each into a clean, specific answer: name tables, routes, files, people and numbers; keep my meaning; never promise what the agent will do. Reply with exactly ten lines numbered 1. to 10. in the order above, one answer per line, so I can paste them straight back into the boxes; where only I can know the answer, write the number and (skip), never drop or renumber a line. Then, on line 11, answer: how many licences should I buy for these settings and the hours it runs on its own? Show the arithmetic from my numbers and the pricing key at the end. In Claude Code, run /standing-answers instead: it writes them back for you.
licenceKey:
PRICING KEY (read from Stripe on 2026-09-21):
- One licence: $20, 10,000 credits.
- One credit pays for one newly notarised receipt (one countersigned batch of your tape); a replay of a receipt already notarised is free.
- Licences needed ≈ (receipts your agent writes per day × days until your stop date) ÷ credits per licence, rounded up; measuring stays free (L0).
- L2 (prepaid expert hours) and L3 (prepaid compute) carry no price yet; size those as UNMEASURED.

questions.title: The blast radius
questions.short: Ceiling: the most your agent may spend or change while you are away?
questions.fill: At most $___ in one change, $___ of model spend a day, ___ rows a minute.
questions.ask: While nobody watches, what is the most your agent may do: the biggest single change in dollars, the model spend in a day, and the database rows it may change in a minute?
questions.teach: Measured: the biggest change, spend and row rate your agent reached, beside your numbers, every overrun shown. Say it loops on a model call overnight: with a $50 day ceiling the record marks the moment spend passed $50. Not measured: what the overrun cost you.

presets.label: Strict: $10 a change, $10 a day, 500 rows a minute
presets.fill: At most $10 in one change, $10 of model spend a day, 500 rows a minute.

presets.label: Standard: $50 a change, $50 a day, 2,500 rows a minute
presets.fill: At most $50 in one change, $50 of model spend a day, 2,500 rows a minute.

questions.tests: the largest mutation, spend and row rate actually seen on the tape; these numbers size how many licences your settings need

questions.title: The demolisher and your halt
questions.short: Never: what must your agent never run alone, and what should happen when it tries?
questions.fill: Never alone: ___, ___, ___. When it tries, my own stop ___ (logs it and goes on / pauses for a person / stops the run).
questions.ask: What must your agent never do without a person there (change the database schema, touch login, billing or secrets, call a model in a loop with no end)? And what does your own stop, a hook or script you control, do when it tries: log it and go on, pause for a person, or stop the run?
questions.teach: Measured: each time your agent reached for something on this list, and how long your own stop took to act. The stop is yours, on your machine.

choice.label: what your own stop does when your agent tries

presets.label: Secrets, prod database, force-push: stop the run
presets.fill: Never alone: .env and credential stores, a production database drop, git push --force. When it tries, my own stop stops the run.

presets.label: Read-only sandbox: stop the run
presets.fill: Never alone: any shell command, any network call, any write outside a sandboxed scratch directory. When it tries, my own stop stops the run.

questions.tests: halts fired, and how long after the crossing

questions.title: The cause: what success means outside the code
questions.short: Proof it worked: what number outside your code shows the work succeeded?
questions.fill: The work succeeded when ___ (a number a customer or your books would see), checked by ___ every ___.
questions.ask: What fact outside your code tells you your agent's work succeeded: a number a customer or your books would see, not a passing test and not the agent's own log?
questions.teach: Not measured, on purpose: the record shows where the work landed, never whether it was good. Name the outside fact, and you can set the two side by side yourself.

presets.label: Orders keep arriving
presets.fill: The work succeeded when orders keep arriving at the usual daily rate, checked by our sales dashboard every morning.

presets.label: The expected row is in the database
presets.fill: The work succeeded when the expected row is in the production database, checked by a query after every run.

questions.tests: UNMEASURED by design: the tape holds where the work landed, never why

questions.title: The plumber: the work your agent owns
questions.short: Its own ground: which tables, routes and files may your agent work alone, for how long?
questions.fill: My agent ___ owns ___ (tables, routes, files, logins) and may ___ with nobody watching, for ___ hours before a person reads the record.
questions.ask: Which tables, routes, files or services does your agent own outright, and what may it do there with nobody watching? Name them so plainly that a stranger could tell, from one line of the record, whether an action was inside or outside.
questions.teach: Measured: every action placed inside or outside the ground you name, as a count anyone can re-run. Not measured: whether the work inside was correct. The ground is the promise, never the quality.
questions.tests: the share of its calls that land on its own pole
questions.unlocks: Answering adds: every action your agent takes, checked against the ground you name here.

questions.title: What only a person decides
questions.short: A person decides: which calls may no program make, and who makes each one?
questions.ask: Which decisions must a person make because no program can settle them (whether a change is correct, fair or wanted), and who is that person for each?
questions.teach: Not measured, and no one can measure it: no test and no smarter model settles whether a program is correct in every case (Rice, 1953). Your answer names the person; the record shows whether each decision reached them.
questions.tests: UNMEASURED by design: whether the work was good is undecidable; the answer names who decides
questions.unlocks: Answering adds: a named person beside every decision the record can show but never judge.

questions.title: The first hour after a trigger
questions.short: 3 a.m.: when an alert fires, who wakes up, and how fast must someone be on it?
questions.fill: Page ___ at ___. You may dispatch Elias Moosman (ThetaDriven's founder) or ___ within ___ hours, paid from my prepaid consulting hours. If ___ (my model provider) slows or blocks my agent, it runs on ___.
questions.ask: When an alert fires at 3 a.m., who gets paged? May we send an outside expert, paid from the consulting hours your licences prepaid? How soon must someone be on it? And where does your agent run if its model provider slows or blocks it?
questions.teach: Measured: who was sent, when they opened the intake bundle and when they arrived, each on time or late against the window you set here. A late arrival is our failure, and the warranty pays for it.

slider.label: how soon someone must be on it

questions.unlocks: Answering adds: a log that marks every call-out on time or late against the window you set.

questions.title: The electrician: the work next to its own
questions.short: Next door: what work beside its own may your agent touch, how far, and who do you call?
questions.fill: Beside its own ground it may touch ___; up to ___ steps outside; then I call ___.
questions.ask: What work next to its own may your agent need (a shared table, another team's service, your servers)? How far outside its ground may it go before your stop rule acts, and who do you call when it does?
questions.teach: Measured: every step outside its ground, how far it went, when it started, and whom you called. Not measured: whether the step was needed. A step outside is a signal to look at, never proof of a fault.

slider.label: how far outside its ground it may go before your stop rule acts

questions.suggestion: providers with landed grip at those cells (C903)
questions.tests: electrician excursions, their distance, who was called, and the semantic vega: how far each landing sat from your declaration (C931)
questions.unlocks: Answering adds: every step outside its ground, counted with how far it went and whom you called.

questions.title: The witness: the record your agent did not write
questions.short: Proof outside logs: what would a stranger need that your agent's own log leaves out?
questions.fill: A stranger would get ___ (the signed record, the commit range). My agent's own log leaves out ___.
questions.ask: If something went wrong, what would you show a stranger, and what does your agent's own log leave out that a stranger would need?
questions.teach: Measured: a record signed by a second key your agent does not hold, so a stranger can re-run it without trusting you or us. A log the agent writes cannot hold what the agent threw away, so the proof is a record the agent did not write. A cloud bot's own screen recording is its own account too.
questions.unlocks: Answering adds: a second signature on the record, so a stranger can check it without trusting you or us.

questions.title: Your policy's wording on AI
questions.short: Your insurance: what does your policy say about AI, and what does it leave out?
questions.fill: My ___ policy with ___ excludes ___ under form ___; my deductible is $___. (The warranty sits beside this gap; it is not insurance.)
questions.ask: What does your current insurance say about AI, and which losses does it leave out? Quote the clause (forms such as CG 40 47, CG 40 48, CG 35 08, or your insurer's own).
questions.teach: Not measured, and not on the record: this is the gap a carrier reads, and the gap our warranty sits beside. The warranty covers our own act; it is not insurance for your loss. A summary drops the exclusion, so quote the clause as written.
questions.tests: nothing on the tape: this is the gap a carrier reads
questions.unlocks: Answering adds: the gap your own policy leaves, named beside what the warranty covers.

questions.title: The level, the scope, and your stop
questions.short: When to stop paying: which failure of ours, checked on what date, makes you walk away?
questions.fill: Trial, ___ licences (or L1). If our act fails, we pay you in kind: API credits we buy for you on ___ (your model provider: Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter) and consulting hours with Elias Moosman, ThetaDriven's founder. I stop paying if ___ (a call-out that arrived late / an alert that did not fire as set / a re-run that gave different bytes / a gap in the record), checked on ___.
questions.ask: Which level do you take: L0 (measure, free), L1 (the licence), or the trial (the minimum licences, consulting hours you use when you like, and a multiple of your licence spend paid back in kind if our act fails)? Which failure of OUR act would make you stop paying, and on what date will you check? You sign that ThetaDriven warrants its own act, never your agent or its results: how well your agent does is your number, not our warranty.
questions.teach: Measured: each failure of our act, read on the date you set: a call-out on time or late against its window, the alert recomputed from your own rows, the re-run bytes against the receipt, the record with no gaps. Your agent's own numbers show beside it, yours to judge, never a ground to claim against us: that would be insurance. On or after your date the badge and /backup/warranty say it is due until you record keep or stop.

date.label: the date you will read your own number

questions.tests: your own number, read on your own date
questions.unlocks: Answering adds: the level you take and the date you check your own number, beside those terms.
